subtopics.title: Write in standard form
subtopics.exposition: A quadratic equation is an equation where the exponent of the variable is at most 2. The equation 2x^2+2x=1 is given as an example of a quadratic equation. The first step in solving a quadratic equation is to rewrite the equation in the required form ax^2+bx+c=0.

subtopics.title: Solve quadratics by factorising
subtopics.exposition: When both factors are the same, as in (x-1)(x-1)=0, the quadratic is a perfect square. Quadratic equations differ from linear equations in that a linear equation has only one solution, while a quadratic equation has at most two solutions. If a times b equals 0, then a=0 or b=0. The solutions of (rx+s)(ux+v)=0 are x=-s/r or x=-v/u, respectively. When the quadratic is a perfect square, there is only one solution to the quadratic equation because both factors are the same. Quadratic equations are solved using factorisation. To solve a quadratic equation by factorisation, write it in its equivalent factorised form; for example, 2x^2-x-3=0 is written as (x+1)(2x-3)=0. Divide the entire equation by any common factor of the coefficients to obtain an equation of the form ax^2+bx+c=0. After dividing out the common factor, a, b and c have no common factors. For example, 2x^2+4x+2=0 can be written as x^2+2x+1=0 after dividing by the common factor. Factorise ax^2+bx+c=0 to be of the form (rx+s)(ux+v)=0. The two solutions come from setting each factor equal to zero: (rx+s)=0 or (ux+v)=0. Check the answer by substituting it back into the original equation. To solve 3x^2+2x-1=0, factorise it as (x+1)(3x-1)=0. After factorising, solve for both factors: x+1=0 gives x=-1, OR 3x-1=0 gives x=1/3. Write the final answer as a statement giving both solutions: the solution to 3x^2+2x-1=0 is x=-1 or x=1/3. An equation written as 0=-2x^2+4x-2 is rearranged to -2x^2+4x-2=0, with zero on the right, before dividing out the common factor to give x^2-2x+1=0. Divide the equation by the common factor: -2x^2+4x-2=0 becomes x^2-2x+1=0. Factorise x^2-2x+1=0 as (x-1)(x-1)=0, which is written (x-1)^2=0. For a perfect square, solve the single repeated factor: (x-1)^2=0 gives x-1=0, so x=1; the solution to 0=-2x^2+4x-2 is x=1.

claims.claim: A quadratic equation is an equation where the exponent of the variable is at most 2.
The equation 2x^2+2x=1 is given as an example of a quadratic equation.
The first step in solving a quadratic equation is to rewrite the equation in the required form ax^2+bx+c=0.
Quadratic equations differ from linear equations in that a linear equation has only one solution, while a quadratic equation has at most two solutions.
There are some special situations in which a quadratic equation has either one solution or no solutions.
Quadratic equations are solved using factorisation.
To solve a quadratic equation by factorisation, write it in its equivalent factorised form; for example, 2x^2-x-3=0 is written as (x+1)(2x-3)=0.
If a times b equals 0, then a=0 or b=0.
Divide the entire equation by any common factor of the coefficients to obtain an equation of the form ax^2+bx+c=0.
After dividing out the common factor, a, b and c have no common factors.
For example, 2x^2+4x+2=0 can be written as x^2+2x+1=0 after dividing by the common factor.
Factorise ax^2+bx+c=0 to be of the form (rx+s)(ux+v)=0.
The two solutions come from setting each factor equal to zero: (rx+s)=0 or (ux+v)=0.
The solutions of (rx+s)(ux+v)=0 are x=-s/r or x=-v/u, respectively.
Check the answer by substituting it back into the original equation.
To solve 3x^2+2x-1=0, factorise it as (x+1)(3x-1)=0.
After factorising, solve for both factors: x+1=0 gives x=-1, OR 3x-1=0 gives x=1/3.
Write the final answer as a statement giving both solutions: the solution to 3x^2+2x-1=0 is x=-1 or x=1/3.
An equation written as 0=-2x^2+4x-2 is rearranged to -2x^2+4x-2=0, with zero on the right, before dividing out the common factor to give x^2-2x+1=0.
Divide the equation by the common factor: -2x^2+4x-2=0 becomes x^2-2x+1=0.
Factorise x^2-2x+1=0 as (x-1)(x-1)=0, which is written (x-1)^2=0.
When both factors are the same, as in (x-1)(x-1)=0, the quadratic is a perfect square.
When the quadratic is a perfect square, there is only one solution to the quadratic equation because both factors are the same.
For a perfect square, solve the single repeated factor: (x-1)^2=0 gives x-1=0, so x=1; the solution to 0=-2x^2+4x-2 is x=1.
